input.strategy_title: Bring-your-own vector database for RAG workloads
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

RAG applications built on Llama Stack need a vector store, and today the
platform neither ships one nor documents how to attach an external one.
Customers are split into two camps with incompatible expectations: regulated
customers want a platform-managed vector database with supported images and
lifecycle, while cloud-native customers already run managed services (e.g.
a cloud vector DB) and only want a sanctioned way to connect them. We have not
decided which posture to productize first, and the answer changes most of the
downstream work.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | A decision is reached, with a documented evaluation, on the first supported vector store posture: platform-managed (operator-deployed Milvus) versus external-connection-only. |
| HLR-2 | P0 | Depending on that decision: either administrators can deploy the managed vector store through the Platform Operator with productized images, or data scientists can register an external vector store connection per project with validated connectivity. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | Llama Stack distributions can consume the chosen vector store as a RAG provider without hand-editing distribution configs. |
| HLR-4 | P1 | The Dashboard exposes the chosen integration (deploy-and-manage UI for the managed path, or connection management UI for the external path). |
| HLR-5 | P2 | Product documentation covers setup and limits for whichever posture ships. |

## Affected Components

- Llama Stack
- Dashboard
- Platform Operator

## Out of Scope

- Shipping both postures in the same release
- Embedding model selection and lifecycle (separate strategy)

## Open Questions

1. Managed Milvus versus external-connection-only is genuinely undecided — the
   evaluation in HLR-1 must weigh supportability cost, disconnected-environment
   viability, and time-to-market, and the outcome forks the implementation
   structure for HLR-2 through HLR-5.

# Midstream repo onboarding for Milvus

## Description

This epic creates the midstream Milvus repository under opendatahub-io so
that the platform can build productized Milvus images. It applies only if the
platform-managed vector store posture is selected. No functional changes to
Milvus itself are in scope — this is repository provisioning only.

## Scope

- Fork/mirror the upstream Milvus repository into a midstream repository
  under opendatahub-io.
- Apply the midstream organization's onboarding conventions (permissions,
  branch protection, ownership, mirroring/sync workflow with upstream).
- Leave the repository ready to serve as the build source for a Konflux
  build pipeline.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A midstream Milvus repository exists under opendatahub-io.
- Upstream mirroring/sync is configured and functioning.
- The repository follows the midstream organization's onboarding conventions
  (access, branch protection, owners).
- The repository is usable as the source for building productized Milvus
  container images.

## HLR Traceability

- Enables HLR-2 (P0, platform-managed variant): administrators can deploy
  the managed vector store with productized images. No HLR maps directly to
  this epic; it is a provisioning prerequisite.

# License validation for Milvus and transitive dependencies

## Description

This epic runs license scanning and clearance for Milvus and its transitive
dependencies ahead of productizing managed Milvus images. It applies only if
the platform-managed vector store posture is selected. A license failure
here changes the dependencies and the approach of the managed deployment,
which is why it gates the operator implementation work.

## Scope

- Run license scanning over the Milvus source tree and its transitive
  dependencies.
- Identify copyleft or otherwise incompatible licenses and the components
  that pull them in.
- Document remediation or exclusion options for any conflicts found.
- Produce a license clearance record supporting a productization decision.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A scan report exists covering Milvus and its transitive dependencies.
- Any license conflicts are identified, with remediation or exclusion
  options documented.
- A clearance decision is recorded (proceed, remediate, or escalate) and
  actionable by the downstream implementation work.

## HLR Traceability

- Enables HLR-2 (P0, platform-managed variant): productized images require
  license clearance. No HLR maps directly to this epic; it is a provisioning
  prerequisite.

# Konflux build-pipeline onboarding for the Milvus midstream repo

## Description

This epic onboards the midstream Milvus repository to Konflux so that
productized Milvus container images can be built and released through the
standard pipeline. It applies only if the platform-managed vector store
posture is selected, and it needs the midstream Milvus repository to exist
first. The pipeline configuration is independent of the Platform Operator
implementation work, which proceeds in parallel.

## Scope

- Create the Konflux application and component configuration for the
  midstream Milvus repository.
- Configure the build recipe that produces a productized Milvus container
  image.
- Configure image publishing to the sanctioned registry.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The Konflux pipeline builds a Milvus container image from the midstream
  repository.
- The pipeline runs green on the repository's default branch.
- The produced image digest is published to the sanctioned registry and is
  available for pinning by the managed vector store deployment.

## HLR Traceability

- Enables HLR-2 (P0, platform-managed variant): "productized images" for the
  managed vector store. No HLR maps directly to this epic; it is a
  provisioning prerequisite.

# Platform Operator deployment and lifecycle for the managed vector store

## Description

This epic extends the Platform Operator so that administrators can deploy
the platform-managed vector store (Milvus) with productized images and full
lifecycle management. It applies only if the platform-managed vector store
posture is selected. It proceeds after license clearance for Milvus
dependencies (a license failure would change the approach) and in parallel
with the Konflux build-pipeline onboarding — the productized image digest is
pinned at execution time rather than being a build-order dependency.

## Scope

- Add Platform Operator support for deploying the managed Milvus vector
  store: a declarative administrator-facing API, reconciliation, and
  lifecycle management (install, upgrade, scale, removal).
- Consume the productized Milvus image by pinned digest from the sanctioned
  registry.
- Operator-managed rollout and rollback behavior appropriate for a
  platform-managed service.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Administrators can deploy the managed vector store through the Platform
  Operator without manual manifest editing.
- The deployment consumes the productized Milvus image, pinned by digest
  from the sanctioned registry (pinned digest available from the build
  pipeline).
- Lifecycle operations (upgrade, scale, removal) are performed through the
  operator without direct manipulation of underlying resources.
- Changes pass the Platform Operator's build pipeline (green).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0, platform-managed variant): administrators can deploy the
  managed vector store through the Platform Operator with productized
  images.

# Llama Stack RAG provider consumption of the managed vector store

## Description

This epic makes Llama Stack distributions consume the platform-managed
vector store as the RAG vector provider without hand-editing distribution
configs. It applies only if the platform-managed vector store posture is
selected, and it builds on the managed deployment capability provided by the
Platform Operator.

## Scope

- Wire the managed vector store as the vector-RAG provider in Llama Stack
  distributions, following Llama Stack's provider-plugin configuration model.
- Make the provider configuration discoverable/defaulted from the platform
  deployment so that no hand-editing of distribution configs is required.
- Validate RAG workflows end-to-end against the managed store.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A Llama Stack distribution uses the managed vector store for RAG (vector
  insertion and retrieval) with no manual edits to distribution
  configuration.
- Provider configuration for the managed store is derived from the platform
  deployment rather than hand-edited per distribution.
- An end-to-end RAG workflow is validated against the managed store.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): Llama Stack distributions can consume the chosen vector store
  as a RAG provider without hand-editing distribution configs.

# Dashboard deploy-and-manage UI for the managed vector store

## Description

This epic exposes the platform-managed vector store in the Dashboard with a
deploy-and-manage user interface for administrators. It applies only if the
platform-managed vector store posture is selected, and it integrates with
the managed deployment capability provided by the Platform Operator (the
Dashboard reads and writes Kubernetes CRs; it owns no data plane).

## Scope

- Add a Dashboard navigation section and resource views for the managed
  vector store.
- Provide administrator deploy-and-manage workflows over the operator's
  custom resources (deploy, view status, manage lifecycle).
- Gate the integration behind a feature flag with defaults configured via
  the Dashboard's configuration conventions.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Administrators can deploy and manage the managed vector store from the
  Dashboard.
- The status of the managed vector store is visible in the Dashboard.
- The integration is behind a feature flag consistent with the Dashboard's
  configuration conventions.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P1): the Dashboard exposes the chosen integration — deploy-and-
  manage UI for the managed path.

  model, with no hand-edited distribution configs.
- Definition of which external vector store types are sanctioned/supported
  for registration.

  project.
- Registration validates connectivity to the external store and reports
  failures clearly.
- Llama Stack distributions in the project consume the registered connection
  for RAG (vector insertion and retrieval) with no manual edits to
  distribution configuration.

  (the strategy leaves this breadth undefined; the implementing team defines
  it as part of this work).

# Decide the first supported vector store posture: platform-managed vs external-connection-only

## Description

This epic resolves the strategy's gating open question: which vector store
posture the platform productizes first — a platform-managed vector database
(operator-deployed Milvus with productized images and lifecycle) or an
external-connection-only posture (a sanctioned way for data scientists to
register customer-managed vector stores per project). The outcome determines
the existence and shape of every downstream implementation epic in this
strategy, so it must be decided and documented before any implementation
work starts.

## Scope

- Produce a documented evaluation comparing both postures against the
  criteria named in the strategy: supportability cost, disconnected-environment
  viability, and time-to-market.
- Assess the platform-managed path: what productizing Milvus entails
  (midstream repository, productized images, lifecycle through the Platform
  Operator) and its ongoing support burden.
- Assess the external-connection path: per-project connection registration
  with validated connectivity against customer-managed stores (e.g. managed
  cloud vector databases), including what "sanctioned" means for support.
- Record the decision with rationale and rejected-alternative tradeoffs, in a
  form the platform can act on (e.g. a decision record attached to the
  strategy).
- Obtain sign-off from product and the affected owning teams.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A documented evaluation exists that compares the platform-managed and
  external-connection-only postures across supportability cost,
  disconnected-environment viability, and time-to-market.
- Exactly one posture is selected and recorded, with rationale and the
  tradeoffs of the rejected alternative.
- The decision record is sufficient to select exactly one downstream
  implementation branch (managed vs external) with no remaining
  posture-level unknowns.
- Product and the affected owning teams have signed off on the selected
  posture.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): a decision is reached, with a documented evaluation, on the
  first supported vector store posture.
